verses.1: And Jacob called his sons and said, “Come here. I will tell you what will be said about you in the days to come.”
verses.2: Hear and obey, sons of Jacob! Hear and obey the words of our father Israel.
verses.3: Ruven, in my arms, you are my strength and my beginning. You are more powerful than anything else.
verses.4: Do not be like the sea that cannot be drained; for you have risen from the beds of your father’s graves. Then you have defiled my holy place.
verses.5: Shim’on and Levi are brothers, like oxen that are sold as livestock.
verses.6: Do not let my soul enter their midst. Do not make me proud of them, for in their midst, one was killed, and they were scattered far away.
verses.7: They were strong and brave, but their journey was difficult. They were scattered among Jacob’s descendants, and they were also spread out throughout Israel.
verses.8: You, Judah, you are holy. Your brothers will worship you. Your enemies will bow down before you. Your sons will worship you.
verses.9: Gur Ariya Yehuda was pursued by his own son. He fell down, like a lion and a dog. Who will create us again?
verses.10: It is not allowed for a Jew to remove hair from his head, from his eyebrows, or from his beard, until he has become like the rest of the people.
verses.11: I forbid the grape to be grown in this city. Let no one pick it; let it remain in the vineyard, covered with leaves and blood from the grapes.
verses.12: My eyes are like those of a goat, and my heart is like those of a lamb from milk.
verses.13: Zebulun will dwell in the depths of the sea. He will be situated near the shores, with his legs on either side.
verses.14: Yishshakar hamor geram rovetz be’in hameshpatayim.
verses.15: And he saw that it was good, and the land was pleasant. So he planted crops in it, and it became a place for farming.
verses.16: They judged their people as one of Israel’s rulers.
verses.17: May there be a snake on the path that leads to the dark dwelling place. Its rider fell from his horse.
verses.18: For your salvation, I cry out to the LORD.
verses.19: He will grieve over us, and he will also be sorrowful.
verses.20: As soon as she offers her blood, he will give her the royal gifts.
verses.21: Nafthali Ayala sent those words of wisdom.
verses.22: Son of Porath Yosef, son of Porath Alayiyn. His daughters walked along the path.
verses.23: And they mocked him, and many of them laughed at him. They humiliated him under the arches.
verses.24: And he sat down in Eitan. His hands were trembling. His seeds were separated from those of Jacob’s master. Then he picked up a piece of wood from Israel.
verses.25: May your father help you, and may He bless you with the blessings of heaven above, along with the blessings of the earth below, and the blessings of all creation.
verses.26: With the blessings of your father, may they bless them forever. May they be blessed until the end of time. May they become the head of Josaphat and a worthy monk for his brothers.
verses.27: In the morning, the lion will eat; by evening, it will divide its food among its cubs.
verses.28: All these are the descendants of Israel, twenty-two in total. This is what their father said to them. And a man blessed them, and through his blessing, they were also blessed.
verses.29: And he commanded them, saying, “I will be gathered to my people. Let them bury me in the tomb that is in the valley of Efrón.”
verses.30: In the valley that lies in the field of inheritance, which is located opposite the spring in the land of Canaan. It was this field that Abraham purchased from Esau as part of his inheritance.
verses.31: They buried Abraham and his wife Sarah. They also buried Isaac and his wife Rebekah. And they buried Leah as well.
verses.32: From the land of the fields and the valley in which the children of Heth lived.
verses.33: And Jacob was able to command his sons. He gathered them together, and they went towards the valley. They gathered around him, and he gathered them all together with his people.
